test_title: PYST 14: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Who is in line to become the first woman Chief Justice of the Supreme Court in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice B.V. Nagarathna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Justice B.V. Nagarathna** is slated to become the **first woman Chief Justice of India (CJI)** in **September 2027**. She was born on **October 30, 1962**.
 
• She was elevated to the **Supreme Court of India** on **August 31, 2021**. Her appointment was part of a historic moment where **nine judges** were sworn in simultaneously to the apex court.
 
• She is the daughter of **Justice E.S. Venkataramiah**, who served as the **19th Chief Justice of India** from **June 1989** to **December 1989**. This makes them the first father-daughter duo to both reach the position of Supreme Court judges and potentially the office of the CJI.
 
• Her tenure as **Chief Justice** is expected to be brief, lasting approximately **36 days**, as she will reach the mandatory retirement age of **65 years** in **October 2027**.
 
• Before her elevation to the Supreme Court, she served as a judge of the **Karnataka High Court**, where she was appointed as an additional judge in **2008** and became a permanent judge in **2010**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Justice Anita Sumanth**: She is currently a judge of the **Madras High Court**. She was appointed as an additional judge in **February 2017** and has a strong background in **Direct and Indirect Taxation laws**.
 
• **Justice Sangeeta Chandra**: She serves as a judge at the **Allahabad High Court**. She was elevated to the bench in **September 2016** and has dealt extensively with **civil and constitutional matters**.
 
• **Justice R. Hemalatha**: She was a judge of the **Madras High Court** who retired in **2021**. She began her judicial career in the **Tamil Nadu State Judicial Service** in **1991** before being elevated to the High Court in **2017**.
 
• **Justice M. Fathima Beevi**: Historically, she was the **first female judge** of the Supreme Court of India, appointed in **October 1989**. However, she never held the post of Chief Justice.
 
• **Article 124**: This article of the **Constitution of India** deals with the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court, including the appointment of judges by the **President of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Seniority Principle**: The appointment of the **Chief Justice of India** usually follows the **seniority convention**, where the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is recommended by the outgoing CJI and appointed by the **President**.
 
• **Collegium System**: Judicial appointments to the Supreme Court and High Courts are made via the **Collegium System**, which consists of the **CJI** and the **four senior-most judges** of the Supreme Court.
 
• **Gender Representation**: Since the inception of the Supreme Court on **January 26, 1950**, there has been a significant gender gap. Out of over **250 judges** appointed to the apex court till date, only a small fraction (around **11**) have been women.
 
• **Retirement Rules**: Under the Indian Constitution, Supreme Court judges retire at **65 years**, while High Court judges retire at **62 years**. This age limit is a critical factor in determining the succession line for the **Chief Justice** position.
 
• **Oath of Office**: Every judge of the Supreme Court is required to take an **oath or affirmation** before the **President** or a person appointed by them, as per the **Third Schedule** of the Constitution.
